As you are aware, communication facilities on or traversing public lands often provide vital public and national defense communication circuits. Continuity of such service is dependent upon immediate access to the lines and other facilities at all times. Further, spurious emissions from radio transmitters could cause destructive electrical interference to communication requirements of others, including harm to common carrier circuits which the Commission is charged with protecting from such interference. It is also possible that such interference could pose risks to safety of life and property.
The foregoing public interest considerations are merely illustrative of those with which the Commission may be concerned and are not intended to encompass all such considerations which we may properly consider in discharging our statutory responsibilities.
Such responsibilities are discharged, in part, via inspections and investigations by Commission employees and other governmental agents in the field, often involving the off-road use of motorized vehicles. It would appear that such operations would be exempt from the proposed restrictions in light of the provision excepting law enforcement vehicles. We believe it imperative that it be made clear that such governmental inspection and investigatory operations will be exempted.
In short, the Commission wishes to stress the necessity for ensuring that whatever regulations are finally promulgated restricting off-road uses of vehicles, adequate provision be made to ensure that vital communication requirements are capable of being duly satisfied at all times.
This letter was adopted by the Commission on July 6, 1972. Commissioner Nicholas Johnson concurring in results; Commissioner Benjamin Hooks absent.
BY DIRECTION OF THE COMMISSION
